sections.title: Identification
sections.text: Agaricus xanthodermus has a white to off-white cap, often rather square in profile when young and broadly convex to flat with age. Scratching the cap edge or cutting and rubbing the swollen stem base produces a rapid chrome-yellow stain, especially in fresh specimens; the yellow may later turn brown. Its crowded free gills are pale at first, then pink and finally dark chocolate to purplish brown. The white stem has a broad persistent hanging ring, often with a ridge beneath it, and no basal cup. A chemical odour of phenol, ink or disinfectant is usually noticeable, especially when cut or heated. The spore print is very dark brown.

sections.title: Habitat and season
sections.text: A saprotrophic mushroom growing on soil in lawns, gardens, parks, hedgerows and other disturbed or grassy places, often in groups. In Britain and Ireland it fruits mainly from summer through autumn; the season varies with climate and rainfall.

sections.title: Similar species
sections.text: The edible field mushroom (Agaricus campestris) also has pink gills that darken but lacks the immediate strong chrome-yellow staining and phenolic smell. Some other Agaricus can yellow slightly, so inspect several features together, especially a freshly cut stem base, gill colour and odour. A closed white button is particularly hard to identify and must not be judged by cap colour alone.

sections.title: Toxicity and surveillance
sections.text: Poisonous: ingestion may cause nausea, abdominal cramps, vomiting and diarrhoea. In the ANSES review of French poison-centre cases for the 2022 picking season, yellow stainers appeared in 25.7% of the 175 meals whose harvest contained at least one toxic species identified by a mycologist; this is not a percentage of all mushroom harvests or of severe poisonings. After suspected ingestion, seek poison-centre or emergency advice and keep any remaining specimens.

traits: White to off-white cap, often somewhat square in profile when young
Cap edge and cut swollen stem base stain rapidly chrome yellow
Free crowded gills pale, then pink, then dark chocolate brown
Broad hanging ring; no volva; dark-brown spore print
Unpleasant phenol, ink or disinfectant odour, especially when cut or heated
safetyNote: Poisonous: can cause nausea, abdominal cramps, vomiting and diarrhoea. A rapid chrome-yellow stain at the cut stem base and a chemical smell are important warning signs. Do not eat; seek poison-centre advice after suspected ingestion.
